lesson_title: The Muffin Stand Truth: One Subtraction Decides Everything
hook_text: Her cash tin held R2 760. Her actual profit? R770. Here's where the money went.
clip_script: Three words carry the whole topic. Income is money flowing in. Expenditure is money flowing out. Profit is what remains when expenditure is subtracted from income. Karabo's month at the sports ground: 165 muffins at R8 is R1 320, plus 120 bottles of juice at R12 is R1 440 — R2 760 in. Now the out side: R1 380 of stock, R300 table rental, R160 electricity, R150 taxi — R1 990 out. The profit line: 2 760 minus 1 990 equals R770. And watch the fifteen muffins she baked but never sold — their ingredients cost R45, spent whether or not anyone buys. Unsold stock quietly eats profit.
visual_style: Animated cash tin filling with green coins, then bills flying out one by one with labels, ending on a glowing R770 — and fifteen sad muffins fading to grey with -R45 above them.
pacing: Quick money-in montage, itemised money-out beats, slow reveal of the profit line and the unsold-stock sting.
